  "text": "Martin found the spare key inside a flowerpot, exactly where his father had insisted nobody would look.

The pot was empty except for gravel and a plastic label that said parsley.

“You ought to move this,” Martin said when he got inside.

His father was sitting at the kitchen table, wearing his coat.

“Then you wouldn’t have found it.”

They were going to buy shoes. The old pair stood beside the radiator, one sole lifting at the toe.

“I could glue that,” his father said.

“You already did.”

“Different glue.”

Martin filled the kettle. There was time before the shops became busy.

On the counter lay a shopping list in his father’s handwriting: milk, pears, polish. Beneath it, in smaller letters, was Martin’s arrival time.

“Did you have breakfast?”

“Of course.”

“What?”

His father looked toward the bread bin.

“Don’t start interviewing me.”

Martin made toast for them both. He cut his own into halves and left the other slices whole.

At the shoe shop, his father rejected three pairs before trying the first again.

“The left one pinches.”

The assistant loosened the laces.

“Now?”

His father walked to the mirror and back.

“That’s better.”

On the way home they stopped for milk and pears. Martin remembered the polish just before the checkout.

“Brown,” his father said.

“I know.”

At the house, Martin put the spare key back under the gravel.

His father watched from the doorway.

“Tuesday?”

“If that suits.”

Inside, his father crossed out the old arrival time. Martin waited while he found a pen that worked."
